I think you ought to try it. I've been in a similar situation, and after a year, I was becoming hypersensitive to every attractive girl that walked past me, and every time a girl started flirting with me. My ex girlfriend was twice as attractive as me and couldn't get down an aisle of a grocery store without getting eyefucked by every guy she walked past.

I more or less "broke up" with her rather than having an open relationship. It was much cleaner for me (clean being lying face down in the shower in the dark hating myself), though still a bit messy in that we still talked a lot. She'd been "getting offers" and wanted to see where they went. In the end though, she called me saying that she felt our relationship was most valuable to her, wanting to get back together; and she was fairly experienced before we started dating.

The point is that feelings are messy. You can try to reign them in, but not without the expense of yourself. When not being involved physically with another person for a while, it's easy to see your vitality slip and melancholy set in. Babies die when fed but not given affection and physical touch.

I don't know how you both feel about each other, so I won't compare your feelings to my ex's; but if you both at least try it for a little while (baby steps, consistent communication, and being honest if you're uncomfortable), you can figure out if it's something that is sustainable. Also, it'd be really helpful if you can mark a date where you change your long distancing to short distancing.

Good luck. I'm honestly kind of sad about this, because I'm reminded of my experience, but hopefully I've been able to help to some increment.
